mcq.q: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
Which statement about TRUNCATE compared with DELETE is correct?
options: TRUNCATE removes all rows at once and cannot take a WHERE clause
TRUNCATE can delete selected rows with WHERE
TRUNCATE fires row-level triggers for every row
mcq.answer: TRUNCATE removes all rows at once and cannot take a WHERE clause

mcq.q: What is the difference between UNION and UNION ALL?
options: UNION removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL keeps them
UNION ALL removes duplicates; UNION keeps them
mcq.answer: UNION removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL keeps them

mcq.q: What is a covering index?
options: An index containing every column a query needs, so the table itself is not read
An index on every column of the table
A clustered index on the primary key
An index that covers all rows but no columns
mcq.answer: An index containing every column a query needs, so the table itself is not read

mcq.q: Why can `WHERE id NOT IN (subquery)` unexpectedly return no rows?
options: If the subquery returns a NULL, every comparison becomes unknown
NOT IN only works on indexed columns
NOT IN is not valid SQL
Subqueries cannot be used with NOT IN
mcq.answer: If the subquery returns a NULL, every comparison becomes unknown

How is optimistic locking usually implemented?

Using SELECT … FOR UPDATE on every read
